table.purpose: t01 is a central entity table (one row per record, ~79,851 rows) referenced by many other tables (t02–t08). Each row pairs an ID with a category label and a timestamp. The exact domain cannot be determined from the data alone; the label column mixes person-role-like values (Student, Teacher, Editor) with topic-like values (correlation, pca, modeling), so the entity type is unresolved. The timestamps fall in a future range (2066–2070), suggesting synthetic or shifted data.

col_001.name: id
col_001.description: Primary key of t01; unique integer identifier for each row. Referenced (as foreign key) by many other tables (t02–t08), making t01 the parent/central table of the database.

col_002.name: parent_id
col_002.description: Integer referencing another row's identifier, joining to t07.col_001 and t03.col_001 (many-to-one). Likely a self-style reference to a parent/related entity in those tables; the exact semantic (e.g., owner, group, category) is not determinable from the data.

col_004.name: created_at
col_004.description: Timestamp per row, mostly unique, ranging 2066-07-19 to 2070-09-14. The future dates indicate synthetic or date-shifted data. Plausibly a creation/event timestamp for the row; the specific event (created, updated, occurred) cannot be confirmed.

table.name: comments
table.purpose: Comments posted on a Q&A site (Stack Exchange-style, likely Cross Validated / stats.stackexchange given content about statistics, whuber, probabilityislogic). Each row is one comment: its text, score, author, and the post it belongs to. Dates appear shifted ~40 years into the future (2065-2070), likely anonymized/scrambled timestamps.

col_001.name: comment_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique identifier of the comment row.

col_002.name: post_id
col_002.description: Identifier of the post (question or answer) the comment was made on; references posts in t03/t05. Many comments share a post.

col_003.name: score
col_003.description: Upvote score of the comment; heavily skewed toward 0 (77% zeros), max 90.

col_004.name: body
col_004.description: Free text of the comment; contains @user mentions, markdown, links, typical Q&A comment phrasing.

col_005.name: created_at
col_005.description: Creation timestamp of the comment. Values fall in 2065-2070, suggesting dates were shifted/anonymized; it is still a per-row creation datetime.

col_006.name: user_id
col_006.description: Identifier of the comment's author; references users (t07). Null for ~1.6% of rows (deleted/anonymous users).

col_007.name: user_display_name
col_007.description: Display name of the author, populated only when the user record is missing/deleted (98.4% null); values like 'user10525' are typical anonymized deleted-account names.

table.name: posts
table.purpose: Post records from a Q&A forum (Stack Exchange-style, content is statistics/Cross Validated). One row per post (question, answer, tag wiki, etc.). Timestamps appear shifted ~40 years into the future, likely anonymization.

col_001.name: post_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique integer identifier of the post. Referenced by many other tables (comments, votes, revisions, etc.).

col_002.name: post_type_id
col_002.description: Small-integer code (1-38, 25 distinct values) referencing lookup tables t01/t02/t05. Dominant values 1-5 match Stack Exchange post types (1=question, 2=answer, 3=wiki, 4=tag wiki excerpt, 5=tag wiki), but the presence of values up to 38 is unexplained; could alternatively be a site/network id. Referenced lookup labels were not provided, so the exact code list is unconfirmed.

col_003.name: parent_post_id
col_003.description: Identifier of the parent post (the question an answer belongs to); references post ids in t02/t05. Null-free but only ~30% unique, consistent with many answers per question. Alternatively a generic related-post reference.

col_004.name: guid
col_004.description: UUID (mostly unique, with a zero-UUID placeholder repeated 169 times) serving as an external/global identifier for the post.

col_005.name: creation_date
col_005.description: Timestamp when the post was created. Values span 2065-2070, i.e. dates shifted into the future (likely anonymized real dates ~2020-2025); the clustering of top values suggests bulk import events.

col_006.name: owner_user_id
col_006.description: Id of the user who owns/created the post; references the users table (t07). Value -1 appears (community wiki / system user); 7% null for posts without a registered owner.

col_007.name: body
col_007.description: Full text content of the post (question or answer body), including markdown, HTML and MathJax; some rows contain only tag-like tokens (e.g. '<regression>', '<r>') for tag wiki posts.

col_008.name: edit_comment
col_008.description: Revision/edit comment (e.g. 'edited title', 'added 186 characters in body'); empty for the majority of posts that were never edited.

col_009.name: owner_display_name
col_009.description: Display name of the post owner when no user account is linked (e.g. 'user10525'); empty when owner_user_id is set.

table.purpose: Likely a transaction/transfer event table: each row records a single event at a timestamp between two entities (col_003 and col_004), with a small status/type flag (col_005). The near-equal values of col_003 and col_004 in some rows (e.g. 25189 vs 25181) suggest paired source/destination identifiers, e.g. from-account and to-account. The entity identifiers appear to reference t05 (statistically accepted join). Overall meaning is tentative; the opaque table/column names and lack of lookup labels prevent stronger conclusions.

col_001.name: transaction_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique integer identifier for each row (event).

col_002.name: event_timestamp
col_002.description: Timestamp of the event, stored as VARCHAR. Dates fall in 2066-2070, which are implausible as real dates, so this is likely synthetic data or a shifted/offset date. The top value repeating 234 times suggests a batch or default timestamp.

col_003.name: source_entity_id
col_003.description: Integer referencing an entity in t05 (statistically accepted many-to-one join; also plausibly t03 or t02). Given paired values with col_004, likely the 'from' side of the event (e.g. originating account).

col_004.name: target_entity_id
col_004.description: Integer referencing an entity in t05 (statistically accepted join). Paired with col_003; likely the 'to' side of the event (e.g. destination account).

table.name: posts
table.purpose: Q&A forum posts (questions and answers) from a statistics Stack Exchange-style site; one row per post, with scores, tags, edit history, and moderation metadata.

col_001.name: post_id
col_001.description: Primary key of the post; unique integer identifier referenced by many other tables.

col_002.name: post_type_id
col_002.description: Post type code referencing a lookup table (t01/t02/t03). Values 1 and 2 dominate (roughly 47.8k answers=2, 42.9k questions=1); rare values 3-7 likely denote wiki/tag-wiki/moderator-type posts.

col_003.name: parent_post_id
col_003.description: Id of the parent question for answer posts; null for questions (84% null overall, consistent with ~53% answers plus orphaned/deleted parents).

col_004.name: creation_date
col_004.description: Timestamp when the post was created (dates appear shifted ~60 years into the future, likely anonymized).

col_005.name: score
col_005.description: Net vote score of the post (upvotes minus downvotes); range -19 to 192, heavily skewed toward small values.

col_006.name: owner_user_id
col_006.description: Id of the user who created the post; null for ~53% of rows (anonymous or deleted accounts). References a users table (t03).

col_007.name: body
col_007.description: Full post body in HTML (questions and answers about statistics, R, regression, probability, etc.).

col_008.name: last_editor_user_id
col_008.description: Id of the user who last edited the post; -1 denotes a system/community-wiki user. References t07 (users).

col_009.name: last_activity_date
col_009.description: Timestamp of the last activity on the post (edit, answer, comment).

col_010.name: title
col_010.description: Post title; only present for questions (null for answers, matching the ~53% answer share).

col_012.name: answer_count
col_012.description: Number of answers on a question; null for answers (53% null matches answer share).

col_013.name: comment_count
col_013.description: Number of comments on the post (0-45, mostly small).

col_014.name: favorite_count
col_014.description: Number of users who favorited/starred the question; null for answers and unfavorited questions (86% null).

col_015.name: view_count
col_015.description: Number of views of the question; null for answers (~51.5% null, close to answer share).

col_016.name: last_edit_date
col_016.description: Timestamp of the most recent edit; null for never-edited posts.

col_017.name: community_owned_date
col_017.description: Date the post became community wiki (97% null, as expected); alternatively could be a closed/locked date, but community-owned fits the rarity and repeated timestamps.

col_018.name: linked_post_id
col_018.description: Id of another post linked to this one (e.g. accepted answer or duplicate/merged post); null for ~48% of rows. The exact semantics (accepted answer vs. duplicate link) cannot be distinguished from the evidence.

col_019.name: deletion_date
col_019.description: Timestamp of a rare moderation event (98% null), paired with col_020; likely deletion, migration, or closure date.

col_020.name: moderator_username
col_020.description: Display name of the user associated with the event in col_019 (e.g. deletion/migration); null rate matches col_019 exactly.

table.name: tags
table.purpose: Glossary/tag table of statistics terminology: each row is a unique statistics term (e.g. "2sls", "stratification", "glmm"), with an id, a term slug, a popularity/usage count, and optional links to related entities in other tables (t02/t03/t05). The exact nature of the linked tables is unknown, so the relationship semantics are unresolved.

col_001.name: term_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique integer identifier for each term row.

col_002.name: term_slug
col_002.description: Unique text label for each row: lowercase hyphenated statistics terms/methods (2sls, ab-test, stratification, glmm, overdispersion). Serves as a natural key/name of the term.

col_003.name: usage_count
col_003.description: Integer, 1..7244, heavily right-skewed (median 29). Plausibly a count of occurrences/uses of the term (e.g. question counts on a stats Q&A site), referencing counts in t01/t03/t05. Could alternatively be a category id; the count-like distribution favors a usage/frequency count, but the referenced tables' content is unknown.

table.name: users
table.purpose: User accounts/profiles of a Q&A community (Stack Exchange-style site): one row per user, with profile fields (display name, website, location, bio, avatar) and activity counters (votes, views). Dates are shifted ~40 years into the future, suggesting anonymized/synthesized data derived from a real Stack Exchange dump.

col_001.name: user_id
col_001.description: Primary key identifying each user row. Unique across all 40,325 rows; referenced by activity tables (t01, t02, t03, t05) that store per-user events/posts.

col_003.name: creation_date
col_003.description: Timestamp when the user account was created. Nearly unique per row, always populated, and always earlier than col_005 for the same row.

col_005.name: last_access_date
col_005.description: Timestamp of the user's last activity/visit; same range as creation dates but per-row later than col_003.

col_006.name: website_url
col_006.description: Personal website URL from the user's profile; ~80% empty, with placeholder values like 'http://none' or 'http://N/A' when absent.

col_007.name: location
col_007.description: Self-reported free-text location from the profile ('United States', 'London, United Kingdom', 'Washington, DC', even 'UTC -6'). ~71% empty.

col_008.name: about_me
col_008.description:
HTML-formatted 'about me' biography from the profile (values wrapped in

tags, contain links and job descriptions). ~77% empty.

col_009.name: up_votes
col_009.description: Count of upvotes cast by the user: heavily zero-skewed (50% zero), max 20,932. Most plausibly the upvote count; could alternatively be another activity counter (e.g. views), but the zero-skewed count pattern fits votes best.

col_010.name: down_votes
col_010.description: Count of downvotes cast by the user: 78% zero, max 11,442. Same ambiguity as col_009; likely the downvote counter paired with col_009.

col_011.name: views
col_011.description: Small activity counter, 98% zero, max 1,920. Could be profile views or a third vote/flag counter; the exact metric is not determinable from values alone.

col_012.name: network_account_id
col_012.description: Unique integer per row (min -1 as a null sentinel), values up to ~5M, uncorrelated with col_001. Matches the pattern of a Stack Exchange network-wide account id stored alongside the per-site user id.

col_013.name: age
col_013.description: Age in years: only ~20% populated, range 13-94, centered around 30 - consistent with a self-reported age field.

col_014.name: profile_image_url
col_014.description: URL of the user's avatar/profile image (gravatar, googleusercontent, facebook graph URLs); the most common value is the default identicon avatar, i.e. users without a custom picture.

table.purpose: A transactional/fact table (38,930 rows) keyed by a surrogate ID, linking entities from t05/t03/t01 via a shared key, with a date and two sparse numeric attributes. Exact domain is unresolved due to opaque names and no lookup labels.

col_001.name: row_id
col_001.description: Surrogate primary key; unique integer 1-43538 with no gaps pattern, referenced by t05.col_013 (many-to-one from t05's side), so each row here can be referenced by rows in t05.

col_002.name: entity_id
col_002.description: Foreign key to a shared entity key (t05.col_001, t03.col_001, t01.col_001 all accept it), i.e. an identifier of some party/object (e.g. customer or account) appearing in multiple tables. 8,584 distinct values, so each entity has on average ~4.5 rows here.

col_003.name: type_code
col_003.description: Small categorical code (10 distinct values, 1-16, dominated by 2 with ~86%). Joins statistically to the same entity key tables, but with only 10 values it more likely encodes a type/status/category of the row. The specific meanings of the codes are unknown.

col_004.name: transaction_date
col_004.description: Date of the event/row, ranging 2066-07-19 to 2067-05-01 (about 9.5 months, 287 distinct days). The future-dated years suggest a shifted/anonymized date axis; treated as a plain date attribute.
